description: Port cfMesh polyMeshGenChecks: a QualityReport over a VolumeMesh — per-cell volumes+centroids (pyramid decomposition), face non-orthogonality (angle between face normal and owner->neighbour centre vector), skewness (face-centre vs cell-line intersection), cell aspect ratio (sum|Sf|/(6 V^2/3), =1 for a cube), min face area, min cell volume, negative-volume cell count. Needed to trust a generated mesh before solving (V&V). Pure Rust. V&V: a Cartesian cube mesh has ~0 non-orthogonality/skewness, aspect ~1, no negative cells; a stretched box has aspect>1; a snapped carve reports finite, non-zero distortion (the metric detects it).
title: cfmesh: mesh quality checks (polyMeshGenChecks analogue)

description:
FOLLOW-UP (maintainer flag 2026-09-10). ScoreType::Absorption is currently approximated as (Sigma_t - Sigma_elastic) because MacroXs has no absorption column (scoring.rs:96). This over-counts by inelastic + (n,2n)/(n,3n) and biases the reactor-physics six-factor consistency_gap positive (measured ~+23% on a fast U-238-heavy pincell in op-mzvp.2.2 tests; the telescoping identity itself is exact).

INVESTIGATION DIRECTION: read the OpenMC C++ + its data path to see how a real absorption XS is assembled, then mirror it into MacroXs/MicroXs:
  - ~/Documents/research/openmc/src/nuclide.cpp, reaction.cpp, cross_sections.cpp, tallies/tally_scoring.cpp (SCORE_ABSORPTION) - how 'absorption' is summed (MT=27? capture MT=101/102 + fission? per-reaction?).
  - ~/Documents/research/openmc/include/openmc/nuclide.h - the XS struct fields (does it carry absorption directly from the ACE/HDF5, or compute it?).
  - njoy-outram-park-fork side: how RECONR/BROADR output is turned into the crate's Nuclide xs_at_energy; whether MT=27 or the capture channels are already reconstructed and just not surfaced on MacroXs.
Then: add MacroXs.absorption (and MicroXs.absorption), populate from the real channels, switch ScoreType::Absorption to use it, tighten CONSISTENCY_BAND back to the reference (-0.005, 0.03). Coordinate with op-6tz.9 / op-6tz.24 (both already ask for this).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
OpenMC absorption mechanism CONFIRMED against source (~/Documents/research/openmc):

- Nuclide::create_derived() (src/nuclide.cpp:358; the XS_ABSORPTION accumulation at :409-417): after 'if (rx->redundant_) continue;' (:402), for every remaining reaction it does XS_TOTAL += xs (:406), then XS_ABSORPTION += xs if is_disappearance(rx->mt_) (:409-411), and for fission adds to BOTH XS_FISSION and XS_ABSORPTION (:413-417). So absorption = sum over NON-REDUNDANT { disappearance reactions + fission }. NOT total - scatter.
- is_disappearance(mt) (src/endf.cpp:59): MT in N_DISAPPEAR..N_DA (101-117: n,gamma / n,p / n,d / n,t / n,3He / n,alpha / ...), OR N_P0..N_AC (600-849 partial charged-particle), OR a few specific multi-particle MTs.
- mt_matches(event_mt, 27) (src/endf.cpp:125) = is_fission(event_mt) || is_disappearance(event_mt)  -- the scoring-time match for an MT=27 tally.
- redundant_ (src/reaction.cpp:38) set from the ACE data (tmp==1); marks aggregate reactions whose partials are also present, skipped to avoid double-counting.

CRATE STATE -- the fix is SMALLER than first thought:
- njoy-outram-park-fork ALREADY produces a real absorption: interface.rs:161 capture_xs() (MT=102); wmp.rs:131 'radiative capture is absorption - fission'; gpu_wmp.rs:72 'Absorption (capture + fission)'.
- outram-mc-libs Nuclide XS struct ALREADY carries 'pub absorption: f64' = capture + fission (nuclide.rs:56, 'transport-side currency'), and the transport collision partition uses it. So Godiva/WMP k_eff is NOT affected by the approximation -- the -341 pcm result stands on real absorption.
- The ONLY consumer of the Sigma_t - Sigma_elastic approximation is ScoreType::Absorption in tally/scoring.rs (track-length track_length_value :96 and collision score_collision :295), because MacroXs (material aggregate) does not carry absorption.

DO: add MacroXs.absorption, aggregate it in Material::macro_xs the same way total/elastic/fission are (Sum_i N_i * nuclide_i.absorption), switch both ScoreType::Absorption arms to use it, tighten reactor_physics CONSISTENCY_BAND back toward (-0.005, 0.03). For the HIGH/ENDF tier verify the reconstructed evaluation sums the non-redundant disappearance MTs + fission (mirror create_derived / redundant handling). Cite the openmc file:line above per the porting rule.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: DONE 2026-09-10 (4a67ed267d). MacroXs.absorption added, aggregated in Material::macro_xs from MicroXS::absorption (capture+fission, already produced by njoy WMP/ENDF). ScoreType::Absorption (track-length scoring.rs:96 + collision :311) switched to it. OpenMC MT=27 mechanism verified + cited (nuclide.cpp:409-417, endf.cpp:59, reaction.cpp:38). Reactor-physics fast-pincell consistency gap +23.1% -> -3.1%; CONSISTENCY_BAND back to (-0.01,0.05). Transport already used real absorption so k_eff unaffected. HIGH/ENDF-tier verification that the reconstruction sums non-redundant disappearance MTs + fission is folded into Phase C (op-mzvp.2.8).

title: Real Sigma_a column on MacroXs - remove the op-6tz.9 absorption approximation

description:
Found 2026-08-11 during the op-cv1c range-literal audit.

src/interfaces/functional_programming/hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs uses
  let upper_bound_pressure = Pressure::new::<megapascal>(100.0 - 1.0e-4);
at 8 sites (lines ~504, 532, 578, 605, 630, 673, 750, 800) and one 100.0 - 1.0e-3 (line ~945) as the upper bracket of its (h,s) iterative solve.

Now that region_fwd_eqn_single_phase accepts exactly 100 MPa (op-cv1c), those epsilon backoffs are very likely vestigial workarounds for the router panic: the (h,s) solver could not evaluate h_ps_eqm at exactly 100 MPa without tripping it. Consequence today: the (h,s) envelope is silently 100 Pa narrower than IF97's, so states in the last 100 Pa below the ceiling are rejected with 'enthalpy too high for hs flash'.

NOT changed by op-cv1c's fix — deliberately out of scope, because these are iterative-solver brackets, not region-router range literals, and widening them needs its own verification run against the (h,s) tables.

SUGGESTED WORK: widen to exactly 100.0 MPa, then re-run cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib hs_flash and record the result. Related: hs_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_1000_bar currently panics because the hs flash produces p = 100000837.65614447 Pa (above the ceiling), which is a separate overshoot bug in the same solver.
title: tampines-steam-tables: hs-flash brackets back off 100 MPa by 1e-4 MPa — likely an op-cv1c workaround
